original_question: Consider the algebraic Costas-array construction families listed in Section 3.2, including the Welch- and Golomb-type families W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5*. Is it true that for every order n > 5 these construction methods are pairwise disjoint, so that no Costas array of that order can be produced by two different methods?
target_in_paper: Problem 10 in Section 5.1 ("Disjointness of the algebraic construction techniques"): "Are the construction methods discussed in Section 3.2 pairwise disjoint for orders n > 5?"
correct_elements: Your draft is aimed at the correct open problem: the paper’s Section 5.1 asks whether the Costas-array construction methods are pairwise disjoint for orders n > 5. The central mathematical content is right: overlap between distinct construction families, fixed order n, and the interpretation that no order-n Costas array should arise from two different methods. The family labels W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5* are also the paper’s standard labels for the Theorems 1–9 families in Section 3.2.
missing_details: The nearest official formulation is Problem 10 in Section 5.1, not a statement in Section 3.2 itself.

Problem 10 literally ranges over all construction methods discussed in Section 3.2. Your draft names the nine theorem-level Welch/Golomb families, but Section 3.2 also includes unpredictably emergent methods G1, G0, W0, RW0, and RG1, so the draft is slightly narrower than the paper’s literal wording.

To be fully stand-alone, the question should define pairwise disjointness as: for each fixed integer n > 5, the sets of Costas arrays of order n produced by two distinct methods have empty intersection.

A stand-alone version should say explicitly that a Costas array means a Costas permutation/array of order n in the sense of Definition 1; the paper uses "Costas arrays" and "Costas permutations" interchangeably.

The official open problem is about the resulting families of arrays, not about the internal finite-field parameters (prime p, exponent m, primitive roots, q = p^m, etc.), so those parameters need not be quantified in the refined question unless one is restating the individual constructions.
refined_question: Let M range over the construction methods listed in Section 3.2 of the paper (in particular the theorem-level families W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5*, and, if one follows Problem 10 literally, the remaining Section 3.2 methods as well). For each integer n > 5, let C_M(n) denote the set of Costas arrays of order n produced by method M. Is it true that C_M(n) ∩ C_{M'}(n) = ∅ for every pair of distinct methods M ≠ M'?
justification: The draft is trying to capture the paper’s explicit open problem on overlap among construction families. Section 5.1 introduces exactly this issue, asks whether the various construction methods ever produce the same Costas array, notes database evidence suggesting distinctness for n > 5, and then states Problem 10 in essentially the same terms. Section 3.2 is the needed nearby context because it gives the exhaustive list of construction methods and labels the theorem-level families W1, W2, G2, G3, G4, W3, G4*, G4**, and G5*, while also showing that Section 3.2 literally contains additional emergent methods beyond the nine named in the draft. Definition 1 supplies the stand-alone meaning of "Costas array" and "order."
